arxiv-2012-13313.title: Very High Energy Emission and Cascade Radiation of Gamma-Ray Burst Afterglows: Homogeneous Versus Wind External Media
arxiv-2012-13313.creator: Xiao-Li Huang, Ze-Rui Wang, Ruo-Yu Liu, Xiang-Yu Wang, En-Wei Liang
arxiv-2012-13313.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Xiao-Li Huang, Ze-Rui Wang, Ruo-Yu Liu, Xiang-Yu Wang, En-Wei Liang. Recent detection of sub-TeV emission from gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) represents a breakthrough in the GRB study. The multi-wavelength data of the afterglows of GRB 190114C support the synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) origin for its sub-TeV emission. We present a comparative analysis on the SSC emission of GRB afterglows in the homogeneous and wind environment in the framework of the forward shock model.

arxiv-2104-02874.title: Document Layout Analysis via Dynamic Residual Feature Fusion
arxiv-2104-02874.description: Abstract The document layout analysis (DLA) aims to split the document image into different interest regions and understand the role of each region, which has wide application such as optical character recognition (OCR) systems and document retrieval. However, it is a challenge to build a DLA system because the training data is very limited and lacks an efficient model.

arxiv-2204-07135.title: Scalable and Robust Self-Learning for Skill Routing in Large-Scale Conversational AI Systems
arxiv-2204-07135.creator: Mohammad Kachuee, Jinseok Nam, Sarthak Ahuja, Jin-Myung Won, Sungjin Lee
arxiv-2204-07135.description: Abstract Skill routing is an important component in large-scale conversational systems. In contrast to traditional rule-based skill routing, state-of-the-art systems use a model-based approach to enable natural conversations. To provide supervision signal required to train such models, ideas such as human annotation, replication of a rule-based system, relabeling based on user paraphrases, and bandit-based learning were suggested.

arxiv-2207-01750.title: Federated Split GANs
arxiv-2207-01750.creator: Pranvera Kortoçi, Yilei Liang, Pengyuan Zhou, Lik-Hang Lee, Abbas Mehrabi, Pan Hui, Sasu Tarkoma, Jon Crowcroft
arxiv-2207-01750.description: Abstract . Mobile devices and the immense amount and variety of data they generate are key enablers of machine learning (ML)-based applications. Traditional ML techniques have shifted toward new paradigms such as federated (FL) and split learning (SL) to improve the protection of user’s data privacy.

arxiv-2302-00780.title: On constraining Cosmology and the Halo Mass Function with Weak Gravitational Lensing. 2023 On constraining Cosmology and the Halo Mass Function with Weak Gravitational Lensing. – A.2
arxiv-2302-00780.creator: Shiming Gu (顾时铭) Marc-Antoine Dor, Ludovic van Waerbeke, Marika Asgari, Alexander Mead, Tilman Tröster, Ziang Yan(颜子昂)
arxiv-2302-00780.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shiming Gu (顾时铭) Marc-Antoine Dor, Ludovic van Waerbeke, Marika Asgari, Alexander Mead, Tilman Tröster, Ziang Yan(颜子昂). The discrepancy between the weak lensing (WL) and the Planck measurements of S 8 {S_{8}} has been a subject of several studies. Assuming that residual systematics are not the cause, these studies tend to show that a strong suppression of the amplitude of the mass power spectrum P ⁡ ( k ) P(k) in the late universe at high k k could resolve it.

arxiv-2305-17567.title: No-Regret Learning in Dynamic Competition with Reference Effects Under Logit Demand
arxiv-2305-17567.creator: Mengzi Amy Guo, Donghao Ying, Javad Lavaei, Zuo-Jun Max Shen
arxiv-2305-17567.description: Abstract This work is dedicated to the algorithm design in a competitive framework, with the primary goal of learning a stable equilibrium. We consider the dynamic price competition between two firms operating within an opaque marketplace, where each firm lacks information about its competitor.

arxiv-2307-00569.title: SSP: Self-Supervised Post-training for Conversational Search
arxiv-2307-00569.creator: Quan Tu, Shen Gao, Xiaolong Wu, Zhao Cao, Ji-Rong Wen, Rui Yan
arxiv-2307-00569.description: Abstract Conversational search has been regarded as the next-generation search paradigm. Constrained by data scarcity, most existing methods distill the well-trained ad-hoc retriever to the conversational retriever. However, these methods, which usually initialize parameters by query reformulation to discover contextualized dependency, have trouble in understanding the dialogue structure information and struggle with contextual semantic vanishing.

arxiv-2310-17815.title: Stability of Inverse Problems for Steady Supersonic Flows Past Lipschitz Perturbed Cones
arxiv-2310-17815.creator: Gui-Qiang G. Chen, Yun Pu, Yongqian Zhang
arxiv-2310-17815.description: Abstract . We are concerned with inverse problems for supersonic potential flows past infinite axisymmetric Lipschitz cones. The supersonic flows under consideration are governed by the steady isentropic Euler equations for axisymmetric potential flows, which give rise to a singular geometric source term.

arxiv-2403-01169.title: Learning Suspected Anomalies from Event Prompts for Video Anomaly Detection
arxiv-2403-01169.creator: Chenchen Tao, Xiaohao Peng, Chong Wang, Jiafei Wu, Puning Zhao, Jun Wang, Jiangbo Qian
arxiv-2403-01169.description: Abstract Most models for weakly supervised video anomaly detection (WS-VAD) rely on multiple instance learning, aiming to distinguish normal and abnormal snippets without specifying the type of anomaly. However, the ambiguous nature of anomaly definitions across contexts may introduce inaccuracy in discriminating abnormal and normal events.

arxiv-2403-09015.title: The Axiom of Choice in the κ \kappa -Mantle
arxiv-2403-09015.creator: Andreas Lietz
arxiv-2403-09015.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Andreas Lietz. Usuba has asked whether the κ \kappa -mantle, the intersection of all grounds that extend to V V via a forcing of size < κ {<}\kappa , is always a model of ZFC \mathrm{ZFC} . We give a negative answers by constructing counterexamples where κ \kappa is a Mahlo cardinal, κ = ω 1 \kappa=\omega_{1} and where κ \kappa is the successor of a regular uncountable cardinal.

arxiv-2404-03003.creator: J. Guy, S. Gontcho A Gontcho, E. Armengaud, A. Brodzeller, A. Cuceu, A. Font-Ribera, H. K. Herrera-Alcantar, N. G. Karaçaylı, A. Muñoz-Gutiérrez, M. M. Pieri, I. arxiv-2404-03003.description: Abstract Baryon Acoustic Oscillations can be measured with sub-percent precision above redshift two with the Lyman- α \alpha (Ly α \alpha ) forest auto-correlation and its cross-correlation with quasar positions. This is one of the key goals of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) which started its main survey in May 2021.

arxiv-2508-11975.title: Chart-CoCa: Self-Improving Chart Understanding of Vision LMs via Code-Driven Synthesis and Candidate-Conditioned Answering Conference: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; November 10–14, 2025; Seoul, Republic of Korea. Proceedings of the 34th
arxiv-2508-11975.creator: Gongyao Jiang, Qiong Luo
arxiv-2508-11975.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gongyao Jiang, Qiong Luo. Vision Language Models (VLMs) often struggle with chart understanding tasks, particularly in accurate chart description and complex reasoning. Synthetic data generation is a promising solution, while usually facing the challenge of noise labels. To address this challenge, we first introduce a chart synthesis pipeline that generates aligned chart-question-answer triplets through code generation and execution, ensuring the reliability of synthetic data without human intervention.

arxiv-2508-19337.title: Finite-volume analysis and universal scaling signatures near the chiral phase transition in (2+1)-flavor QCD
arxiv-2508-19337.creator: \firstname Sabarnya \lastname Mitra \fnsep, \firstname Frithjof \lastname Karsch
arxiv-2508-19337.description: Abstract For quantifying the universal properties of the chiral phase transition in QCD through numerical calculations on a discrete space-time lattice, one needs to perform controlled extrapolations to the continuum and infinite-volume limits followed by an extrapolation to the limit of massless light quarks. We discuss here, the results on the latter two limits at still finite lattice spacings.

arxiv-2510-01775.title: Self-Sustained Oscillations of a Nonlinear Optomechanical System in the Low-Excitation Regime
arxiv-2510-01775.creator: Shivangi Dhiman, K. Rubenbauer, T. Luschmann, A. Marx, A. Metelmann, H. Huebl
arxiv-2510-01775.description: Abstract Manifesting across all time, mass and length scales, nonlinearities lie at the core of numerous physical phenomena. Next-generation quantum applications, such as quantum sensing, require the combination of nonlinearity with non-classical correlations. This necessitates the search for an experimental platform which enables a nonlinear response at ultra-low excitation levels in a system with practical sensing potential and quantum compatibility.

pmc-11509018.title: Evaluation of the Role of Tanshinone I in an In Vitro System of Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2N
pmc-11509018.creator: Jingjing Zhang, Xinru Meng, Qianni Qin, Yali Liang, Guangpu Yang, Shen Li, Xiaorong Li, Ji-Chang Zhou, Litao Sun, Walter Herzog
pmc-11509018.description: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2N (CMT2N) is an inherited nerve disorder caused by mutations in the alanyl-tRNA synthetase (AlaRS) gene, resulting in muscle weakness and sensory issues. Currently, there is no cure for CMT2N. Here, we found that all five AlaRS mutations in the aminoacylation domain can interact with neuropilin-1 (Nrp1), which is consistent with our previous findings.

pmc-11611186.title: The relationship between visitors’ motivation and landscape preference for the pilgrimage route on the Mount Miaofeng, China
pmc-11611186.creator: Meijing Xu, Jianjiao Liu, Ru Wang, Shan Lu, Feng Xu, Qianda Zhuang, Qianda Zhuang, Qianda Zhuang, Qianda Zhuang
pmc-11611186.description: Many countries have recognized the significance of religious tourist destinations and actively included them into tourism systems. This study took the pilgrimage route on the Mount Miaofeng, a famous sacred place in northern China, as the research site to comprehensively understand visitors’ on-site experience when walking along it.

pmc-12415213.title: A genome-scale drug discovery pipeline uncovers therapeutic targets and a unique p97 allosteric binding site in Schistosoma mansoni
pmc-12415213.creator: Dylon R. Stephens, Ho Yee Joyce Fung, Yan Han, Jue Liang, Zhe Chen, Joseph Ready, James J. Collins
pmc-12415213.description: SignificanceSchistosomes cause widespread infections in humans, leading to severe chronic illnesses in endemic regions. There is no vaccine for schistosomiasis, and there has been limited success using the current standard-of-care treatment, praziquantel. Therefore, it is essential to identify drug targets within these parasites.

pmc-12505732.title: Roles of TGF-β in the therapeutic potential of hypoxic mesenchymal stem cells for treating osteoarthritis in a Rabbit model
pmc-12505732.creator: En-Rung Chiang, Kun-Hui Chen, Hsuan-Hsiao Ma, Jung-Pan Wang, Hsiao-Li Ma
pmc-12505732.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundOsteoarthritis (OA) is the most prevalent musculoskeletal disease worldwide. Cell-based therapies have emerged as a promising approach for OA therapy. The therapeutic potential of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) has been demonstrated in a wide array of inflammatory diseases. A previous study demonstrated that the injection of the allogeneic MSCs cultured under hypoxia could reduce the progression of osteoarthritis in an anterior cruciate ligament transection (ACLT) model of OA in rabbits.

pmc-12559423.title: Correlation of three wear testing methods and surface roughness analysis in 3D-printed crown materials
pmc-12559423.creator: Anastasiia Grymak, Kai Chun Li, Andrew B Cameron, Sunyoung Ma
pmc-12559423.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The objective of this in vitro study was to evaluate and correlate the wear resistance of three additively manufactured dental restorative materials using three wear test methods. ball-on-disc, block-on-ring, and linear reciprocation. Three polished or glazed restorative materials were divided into four groups and subjected to wear testing under 49 N and 70 N loads, submerged in artificial saliva to simulate 48 months of in vivo wear. Vertical loss, step-height, surface roughness and friction coefficient were recorded.

pmc-12606974.title: The effects of progesterone supplementation in pregnancies assessed by doppler ultrasound: a systematic review of maternal and perinatal outcomes
pmc-12606974.creator: Somayeh Khanjani, Sheida Bashiri Goodarzi, Mohammad Mehdi Khaleghi, Seyyede Sepide Ashraf Moosavi, Reza Eshraghi, MohammadSaeed Soleimani Meigoli, Mobina Fathi, Maryam Nasr Azadani, Nazanin Sadraei, Ashkan Bahrami
pmc-12606974.description: BackgroundProgesterone is essential for pregnancy maintenance, but its effects on complications like intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), preeclampsia, prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM), preterm birth, and placental abruption are still debated. This review investigates the effects of progesterone supplementation on Doppler ultrasound indices and pregnancy outcomes.

pmc-13490431.title: Effectiveness of Hybrid Surgery Using Polyetheretherketone Rods for Preventing Proximal Junctional Kyphosis and Failure After Adult Spinal Deformity Surgery: Biomechanical Evaluation
pmc-13490431.creator: Chao Li, Yao Zhao, Xiangning Meng, Longtao Qi, Beiyu Xu, Chunde Li
pmc-13490431.description: Proximal junctional kyphosis (PJK) and proximal junctional failure (PJF) are common complications of adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery. Hybrid fixation techniques have emerged as a potential solution to mitigate this risk. However, the biomechanical benefits of hybrid rod fixation in long-segment spinal surgery have not been fully explored or validated.

pmc-13494596.title: BioMaster: Multi-agent system for automated bioinformatics analysis workflow
pmc-13494596.creator: Houcheng Su, Junning Feng, Yawen Lu, Yucheng Xu, Jinming Yang, Haojie Lu, Jixin Yang, Xu Yang, Sirui Xie, Weicai Long, Chengrui Wang, Yusen Hou, Tingyu Zhu, Yanlin Zhang
pmc-13494596.description: SummaryThe growing volume and complexity of biological data have made bioinformatics workflows increasingly labor-intensive, error-prone, and difficult to scale. Large language model-based agents offer potential for automation but often fail in complex, multi-step analyses because of limited robustness. We present BioMaster, a multi-agent framework that integrates workflow planning, execution, error recovery, and output validation.
